mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 7 Series 745i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 7 Series 745i engine replacement cost depends on the generation and engine code. N62B44 replacements for E65 models typically range from £1,800-£3,500 for used units, £3,500-£6,000 for reconditioned, and £4,500-£7,500 for rebuilt with warranty. Older M60B40 and M62B44 engines are generally cheaper to replace, while the rare M102/M106 turbo engines require specialist sourcing.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of valve stem seal failure in a BMW 7 Series 745i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common symptom is blue or white smoke from the exhaust on cold startup, clearing after a few seconds. As the seals worsen, you may notice increased oil consumption between services, a slight misfire on startup, and eventually the engine warning light may illuminate.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 7 Series 745i?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - if your BMW 7 Series 745i is otherwise in good condition, a rebuilt engine from £3,500-£7,500 is often worthwhile. With 745i values ranging from £3,000-£15,000 depending on generation and condition, replacement cost typically represents a reasonable proportion of the vehicle's value.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 7 Series 745i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most BMW 7 Series 745i engine replacements take 1-3 days for supply and fit at a specialist garage. The complexity varies by generation - older M102/M106 turbo engines require more specialist attention, while N62 V8 replacements are more routine for BMW specialists.

mainEntity.name: Do BMW 7 Series 745i replacement engines come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - every rebuilt BMW 7 Series 745i engine supplied through EnginesMarket comes with a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines typically have 3-6 month warranties, while reconditioned units often include 6-12 months of cover.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 745i and 750i engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW 745i has always been the entry-level V8 7 Series (or turbo straight-six in the E23 era), while the 750i sits above it with a larger, more powerful engine. In the E65 generation, the 745i uses a 4.4-litre V8 (N62B44, 333hp), while the 750i uses a 4.8-litre V8 (N62B48, 360hp). In the E32 era, the 745i used a 4.0-litre V8 (M60B40, 286hp) while the 750i used a 5.0-litre V12 (M70B50, 300hp).

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 7 Series 745i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 745i badge has been one of the most prestigious in the 7 Series lineup since its debut in 1980. Over four generations, the 745i has been powered by some of BMW's most significant engines - from the turbocharged M102 and M106 straight-sixes of the E23 era through to the naturally aspirated V8s that defined the E32, E38 and E65 generations. The 745i nameplate was retired after the E65, making it a sought-after badge among BMW enthusiasts.

milestones.description: E23 745i, M102B32 3.2L turbo straight-six, 252hp, KKK turbocharger
E23 745i gains M106B35 3.4L turbo straight-six, 252hp, Bosch Motronic
End of E65 745i production; nameplate retired

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 7 Series 745i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 7 Series 745i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 7 Series 745i has been powered by some of BMW's most advanced engines over its history, but each generation has its own well-documented weak points. The most common problems driving 745i replacement searches are N62 valve stem seal failure on E65 models, M62 timing chain guide wear on E38 examples, and age-related turbocharger issues on E23 cars. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: N62 Valve Stem Seal Failure - Why the BMW 7 Series 745i N62B44 Burns Oil
problems.rootCause: The N62's valve stem seals harden and lose their sealing ability over time, allowing oil to seep past the valves and burn in the combustion chamber. This is most noticeable as blue or white smoke on cold startup.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of all 32 valve stem seals; cylinder head remains on engine
repairOptions.longevity: Cost-effective fix if caught early; resolves oil consumption

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, rebuilt N62 with upgraded seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If oil burning has caused catalytic converter damage or if engine is high-mileage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 7 Series 745i (E65) ranges from £3,000-£8,000 depending on condition and mileage. For an E65 745i valued under £5,000, valve stem seal replacement at £1,800-£3,200 is often the better financial decision than a full engine replacement. For cars in exceptional condition, a rebuilt N62 with upgraded seals can be a sound long-term investment.
problems.recommendation: If your BMW 7 Series 745i emits smoke on startup but runs smoothly otherwise, valve stem seal replacement is almost always the right call. This is a well-understood repair that specialist BMW indies perform regularly, and it costs significantly less than a full engine replacement.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N62B44 BMW 7 Series 745i engine prices

problems.h4: M62 Timing Chain Guide Wear - The E38 745i's Achilles Heel
problems.affectedModels: BMW 7 Series 745i (M62B44, E38 generation, select markets)
problems.rootCause: The M62's timing chain guides are made of plastic that becomes brittle with age and heat cycling. When they break, the timing chain can slip or snap, causing catastrophic valve and piston damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of timing chain, guides and tensioners
Supply & fit, rebuilt M62 with upgraded guides, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If chain has slipped causing valve or piston damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: E38 745i values typically range from £3,000-£8,000. Timing chain guide replacement at £1,500-£2,800 is well within the vehicle's value and strongly recommended. A full engine replacement on an E38 745i is rarely cost-effective unless the car is in exceptional condition.
problems.recommendation: M62 timing chain guide failure is well-documented and often catastrophic. If your E38 745i has over 80,000 miles and no record of timing chain work, we recommend preventative replacement - it's far cheaper than a new engine.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M62B44 BMW 7 Series 745i engine prices

problems.h4: E23 Turbocharger and Fuel System Ageing - Classic 745i Reliability
problems.rootCause: The M102 and M106 turbochargers are now over 35 years old. Common issues include turbo bearing wear, oil seal failure, and age-related degradation of fuel injection systems (L-Jetronic on M102, Motronic on M106).

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Rebuild of KKK turbocharger with new bearings and seals
Fuel injection system refurbishment or replacement
Supply & fit, rebuilt M102/M106 with rebuilt turbo, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If internal engine damage has occurred

problems.vehicleValueCheck: E23 745i values vary widely - from £3,000 for a project car to £15,000+ for a well-preserved example. For a high-value example, a rebuilt engine with a refurbished turbocharger is a sound investment. For a lower-value car, consider the repair cost relative to the car's overall condition and value.
problems.recommendation: E23 745i ownership requires specialist knowledge and access to specialist parts. Before committing to a full engine replacement, have a classic BMW specialist assess the turbocharger and fuel system - sometimes the fix is simpler than it first appears.
